title: Superpixel-Based QUBO for Scalable Quantum-Enhanced Medical Image Segmentation
authors: Mohammad Chalhoub, Mahdi Chehimi, Laia Domingo, Omar Alhussein, Ahmed Farouk, Saif Al-Kuwari
abstract: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) has emerged as a powerful framework for medical computing problems. Binary decision variables naturally represent clinical choices, making QUBO formulations well-suited for quantum annealing hardware. However, a fundamental scalability challenge limits practical deployment: problem size grows rapidly with input dimensionality, creating computational bottlenecks that restrict applications to simplified scenarios. This paper addresses this challenge through hierarchical problem reduction, as demonstrated in medical image segmentation, where pixel-level QUBO formulations create over 65,000 variables for a 256x256 image, forcing existing approaches to downsample to 42x42 resolution and discard 97% of pixel information. A superpixel-based QUBO framework is proposed using simple linear iterative clustering (SLIC) to group pixels into perceptually meaningful regions, then formulate segmentation as QUBO over a region adjacency graph (RAG) combining min-cut and smoothness objectives. Validation on INbreast mammography breast cancer images demonstrates a 4.2% improvement in segmentation quality (mean IoU 0.76 vs 0.73) with 33 computational speedup (0.67s vs 21.97s) and a 97.3% reduction in problem size (1764 to 48 variables), all achieved while processing full-resolution images rather than downsampled versions. The reduced problem size also fits well within current quantum annealer connectivity limits, removing the embedding overhead that has historically blocked direct deployment of pixel-level QUBO segmentation on quantum hardware.
summary: This paper introduces a superpixel-based framework to solve medical image segmentation using Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO). By clustering pixels into perceptually coherent regions, the authors drastically reduce the problem size from tens of thousands of variables to dozens while preserving full resolution. This results in superior segmentation quality and massive computational speedups, making quantum optimization feasible for real-world clinical data.
main_problem: The core problem is performing high-fidelity medical image segmentation, specifically on mammography images, which requires processing large amounts of pixel data.
main_result: The superpixel-based QUBO framework significantly improved segmentation quality (4.2% relative IoU improvement) and achieved a 33x speedup compared to pixel-level methods while drastically reducing the problem size for quantum solvers.
method: A novel approach uses SLIC clustering to group pixels into perceptually meaningful superpixels, which are then used to construct a Region Adjacency Graph (RAG). The segmentation objective is formulated as a QUBO over this graph structure.
model_or_system: The model is the Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) formulation of an energy function that combines min-cut and smoothness objectives. This framework is designed to map directly onto quantum annealing hardware, utilizing binary variables representing superpixel labels.
key_observables: Mean Intersection over Union (IoU), Mean Dice Coefficient, computational runtime (seconds), and the size of the QUBO matrix/number of variables.
important_parameters: Superpixel count ($K=60$), smoothness hyperparameter ($\alpha=10$), Gaussian kernel scale parameter ($\sigma$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that grouping pixels into superpixels preserves enough structural information to allow for accurate segmentation, overcoming the data loss inherent in simple downsampling techniques.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the entire pipeline: SLIC clustering $ightarrow$ RAG construction with Gaussian weights $ightarrow$ QUBO formulation $ightarrow$ Optimization $ightarrow$ Final Segmentation Mask. Comparisons show visual improvements over pixel-level artifacts.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of identifying the limitation (scalability of pixel-QUBO), proposing the superpixel solution using SLIC and RAG, detailing the mathematical QUBO formulation derived from graph objectives, validating this method on mammography images against baselines, and concluding with performance metrics.
why_interesting: While the core application is in medical imaging (CV/ML), the methodology involves mapping a complex combinatorial optimization problem onto a QUBO structure suitable for quantum annealers. The successful reduction of variables while maintaining fidelity is highly relevant to scaling up any NISQ-era quantum algorithm implementation.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Superpixel-based QUBO segmentation pipeline. (1) Input mammography image undergoes quantum-inspired contrast-enhancement preprocessing. (2) SLIC algorithm generates 50 superpixels from 65,536 pixels. (3) Region Adjacency Graph connects adjacent superpixels with similarity-weighted edges. (4) QUBO formulation models segmentation as a graph cut with Gaussian weights. (5) Simulated annealing optimizes the binary labeling. (6) Full-resolution segmentation mask isolates the tumor region. The pipeline reduces problem complexity by 97.3% while maintaining image fidelity.

Fig. 2. Visual comparison of pixel-level and superpixel-level QUBO segmentation on mammography image (idx=7). Top row: Pixel-level baseline on 42×42 downsampled image shows blocky artifacts. Bottom row: Superpixel approach on full 256 × 256 resolution preserves fine anatomical details. Overlay shows correct predictions (yellow), false positives (red), and false negatives (green).
